candidates.title: Union protests as CSX plans to cut or furlough maintenance-of-way workers
candidates.excerpt: NOVI, Mich. — CSX is planning to abolish 165 maintenance-of-way positions and furlough more than 1,000 workers, the Brotherhood of Maintenance of Way Employes Division has announced. In a post on its website earlier this month, the union, part of the International Brotherhood of Teamsters, said the furloughs will include approximately 900 BMWED members on track gangs that are not expected to restart until February. It also cited one location where plans call for four employees to be responsible for a 142-mile section of mainline track and multiple yards — territory currently handled by a dozen workers. “Our members know what happens when CSX eliminates positions and spreads the remaining workforce across larger territories,” BMWED General Chairman Brian Thompson said. “The work does not disappear. candidates.title: OOCL launches new China-Cambodia-Thailand service
candidates.excerpt: OOCL will launch a new container service connecting South China with Cambodia and Thailand in October. The new China Cambodia Thailand Service (CCT4) will begin operations on 23 October 2026. CCT4 connects four Asian ports The service will provide direct connections between Nansha and Shekou in South China, Sihanoukville in Cambodia and Songkhla in Thailand. The full port rotation will be: Nansha – Shekou – Sihanoukville – Songkhla – Nansha OOCL said the service will provide additional capacity between the three markets. It is also designed to offer greater flexibility and competitive transit times for cargo moving between South China and Southeast Asia. The carrier said the new connection responds to growing trade demand between China, Cambodia and Thailand. No details regarding the vessels or capacity to be deployed on CCT4 were announced.

candidates.title: Etihad Rail launches Fujairah-Abu Dhabi container service with AD Ports
candidates.excerpt: Etihad Rail and AD Ports Group have launched a direct rail freight service connecting Fujairah Terminals with the Industrial City of Abu Dhabi (ICAD). The new service will transport containers around 200 km between Fujairah and Abu Dhabi. It will initially operate three times per week. The partners have also established ICAD as a customs-enabled inland cargo gateway. Containers can clear customs at ICAD Under the new system, containers arriving at Fujairah Terminals can move directly by rail to ICAD. Cargo can then undergo inspection, customs clearance and release in Abu Dhabi. This brings port-related services closer to manufacturers, warehouses and distribution facilities in the industrial area. ICAD has also received its own UN/LOCODE, AECAD. According to Etihad Rail and AD Ports, shipping lines, freight forwarders and cargo owners can now book cargo directly to ICAD as the destination and clearance point. candidates.excerpt: DP World Cochin handled a record 97,952 TEUs in August 2026, marking the highest monthly container throughput in the terminal’s history. Volumes at the International Container Transshipment Terminal (ICTT) increased 51% compared with August 2025. Container volumes reach new high The August performance followed two months of strong container traffic at the terminal. ICTT handled 74,644 TEUs in June and 74,585 TEUs in July. Throughput then climbed to 97,952 TEUs in August. DP World said the performance reflects the terminal’s growing role in regional and international trade. The terminal also handled 51 ad hoc vessel calls between June and August. According to DP World, the additional calls came as shipping lines adjusted cargo flows amid geopolitical disruptions. candidates.title: Hong Kong shifts port strategy from volume to value
candidates.excerpt: Hong Kong is shifting the development strategy of its container port from volume growth towards higher-value maritime and logistics services under the city’s first Five-Year Plan for Economic and Social Development. The 2026–2030 plan sets out a new direction for Hong Kong Port, with the government aiming to stabilise container throughput while increasing the value generated by the wider maritime and logistics sector. The government described the strategy as a transition from “volume based to value driven development”, targeting a broader “volume to value” transformation of the port. Kwai Tsing targets smart and green transformation A central part of the strategy will be the modernisation of the Kwai Tsing Container Terminals. The government plans to work with terminal operators on a roadmap for their smart and green transformation, including greater use of autonomous electric vehicles, remotely controlled cranes and onshore power supply facilities. candidates.title: ClarkSea Index surges 27% above 2007 peak
candidates.excerpt: Clarksons’ cross-sector ClarkSea Index continues to record new all-time highs as strong conditions spread across gas carriers, bulkers, containerships and car carriers to go alongside the extraordinary earnings seen in the crude tanker sector. The ClarkSea Index climbed another 14% on Friday to $64,569 a day, propelled by record crude tanker earnings but with Clarksons stressing that conditions across the VLGC, bulk carrier, containership and car carrier markets are also at “exceptional or strong levels”. The latest reading puts today’s market well beyond the peaks associated with shipping’s celebrated 2007-08 boom. Clarksons data show the old ClarkSea record was $50,714 a day in December 2007, with the 2008 maximum fractionally lower at $50,402 a day. Today’s index is already 27% above the previous high-water mark. Tankers remain the headline act thanks to the ongoing war between the US and Iran. candidates.title: Rail freight slides in rare off-week

Just three of 10 carload commodity groups improved: Grain, 17.3%; petroleum and petroleum products, 6.5%; and forest products, 2.1%. Motor vehicles and parts led decliners, down 18.8%, followed by chemicals, 9.2%, and nonmetallic minerals, 6%. The Surface Transportation Project Delivery Program allows a State to assume FRA's environmental responsibilities for environmental review, consultation, and compliance under the National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) for railroad projects should a State first assume NEPA responsibilities under the Federal Highway Administration (FHWA). When a State assumes these Federal responsibilities, the State becomes solely responsible and liable for carrying out the responsibilities it has assumed, in lieu of FRA. This program mandates annual audits during each of the first 4 years of State participation to ensure compliance with program requirements.

candidates.title: BNSF, CPKC, and CSX to request broad access to a combined UP-NS network
candidates.excerpt: BNSF Railway, CPKC, and CSX plan to seek broad trackage rights over a combined Union Pacific-Norfolk Southern system, if federal regulators approve the transcontinental merger. Notably, CPKC and CSX are targeting the same corridor: They want access to the Kansas City-St. Louis trackage now controlled by UP or NS, arguing that the merger partners’ existing fix — trackage rights for Canadian National — doesn’t restore meaningful competition. The railroads outlined their plans in Wednesday regulatory filings with the Surface Transportation Board. The filings tip their hands regarding so-called responsive applications the railroads expect to submit by a Nov. 18 deadline. Numerous short line railroads filed similar requests for trackage rights and, in some cases, access to local customers. All three Class I railroads urged the STB to reject the UP-NS merger outright, saying it will harm competition, hurt the economy, and is not in the public interest. But if the board does approve the $85 billion deal, the railroads said regulators should impose numerous conditions to mitigate potential competitive harms. “If the Board decides to go down the path of allowing this merger to fundamentally transform the industry, then it must also fundamentally transform the industry with commensurate conditions to lessen the blow to shippers and the American public,” BNSF told the STB. “To be clear, c

candidates.excerpt: The Greenbrier Companies will transition to new executive leadership in January, with Chief Executive and President Lorie Tekorius set to retire following the company’s 2027 annual shareholders meeting. Brian Comstock, Greenbrier’s executive vice president and president of The Americas, will immediately become president and CEO. The Lake Oswego, Ore.-based railcar manufacturer and freight-transportation services provider (NYSE: GBX) said the move is the result of the board’s long-term succession-planning process. Tekorius’ retirement will become effective Jan. 6, 2027. Tekorius has spent more than 30 years at Greenbrier, joining the company in 1995 and moving through senior financial and operating roles before becoming president and CEO in 2022. She previously served as chief operating officer and as chief financial officer. candidates.title: STB extends deadline for participation in UP-NS merger review
candidates.excerpt: The Surface Transportation Board has extended the deadline for filing notices of intent to participate in the Union Pacific-Norfolk Southern merger to Sept. 30, the board’s chief counsel, Anika S. Cooper, said in a decision on Monday. The deadline had been Sept 4. The change comes at the request of the National League of Cities, which said in an Aug. 26 letter to the board that there are an estimated 12,000 local governments in communities served by railroads, and that many have yet to determine if they will participate. The NLC noted that the original deadline was set Aug. 18 and the original date overlaps a period when many people are on vacation, as well as the Labor Day holiday weekend. The STB said it considers the request to be reasonable and granted it. Other deadlines established in the Aug. 18 decision regarding UP (NYSE: UNP) and NS (NYSE: NSC) are unchanged. candidates.title: Vance, EPA chief call for investigation into Biden administration response to East Palestine derailment
candidates.excerpt: Vice President JD Vance and the head of the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency have asked the EPA’s Office of Inspector General to investigate the Biden administration’s response to the February 2023 Norfolk Southern derailment and hazardous-materials release in East Palestine, Ohio. The EPA said in a Friday, Aug. 28, release that Vance and Administrator Lee Zeldin had sent a joint letter to the OIG asking for the investigation in light of a report released last week by a watchdog group, the Government Accountability Project. That report says initial Department of Defense modeling projected mass casualties from the vent-and-burn disposal of vinyl chloride — information that was withheld from those at the site. An initial estimate projected that 18,000 people could suffer harmful chemical exposure and that 1,900 people were in a “death possible” zone. candidates.title: Permitting Use of Computer-Based, Three-Dimensional Simulation for Periodic Refresher Training on Brake Systems
candidates.source: Federal Register (Transportation Department, Federal Railroad Administration)
candidates.excerpt: Permitting Use of Computer-Based, Three-Dimensional Simulation for Periodic Refresher Training on Brake Systems. Transportation Department, Federal Railroad Administration. Rule. This rule permits railroads to use a simulation that is instructor-led, computer-based, and three-dimensional (3D) to satisfy the hands-on portion of periodic refresher training under FRA's brake system training requirements, consistent with waivers FRA has granted to date. This computer-based 3D simulation training can provide employees with randomized scenarios that may not be readily available for hands-on training and facilitate real-time feedback on performance of duties.

candidates.title: Repealing Outdated Railroad Workplace Safety Requirements and Making Other Improvements
candidates.source: Federal Register (Transportation Department, Federal Railroad Administration)
candidates.excerpt: Repealing Outdated Railroad Workplace Safety Requirements and Making Other Improvements. Transportation Department, Federal Railroad Administration. Rule. This rule repeals several roadway workplace safety requirements that have become obsolete. In addition, FRA establishes a new special approval procedure to enable regulated entities, after public notice and FRA approval, to utilize an alternative approach to bridge worker safety that provides for an equivalent or better level of safety. Also, this rule clarifies that the required training for operators of roadway maintenance machines equipped with a crane includes specific aspects such as maintaining vertical clearance.

candidates.source: Federal Register (Transportation Department, Federal Railroad Administration)
candidates.excerpt: Amendments to Brake System Maintenance and Inspection Requirements. Transportation Department, Federal Railroad Administration. Rule. This rule amends mechanical equipment safety standards related to brake inspections for passenger and freight rail equipment and incorporates longstanding waivers for locomotive brake system maintenance and inspection requirements. The amendments are consistent with the mandates of the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (IIJA), which require FRA to review and analyze certain longstanding waivers to determine whether incorporating the waivers into FRA's regulations is justified, and Executive Order 14219, Ensuring Lawful Governance and Implementing the President's "Department of Government Efficiency" Deregulatory Initiative.

candidates.title: Regulatory Relief From Locomotive Horn Sounding Pattern at Public Highway-Rail Grade Crossings
candidates.source: Federal Register (Transportation Department, Federal Railroad Administration)
candidates.excerpt: Regulatory Relief From Locomotive Horn Sounding Pattern at Public Highway-Rail Grade Crossings. Transportation Department, Federal Railroad Administration. Rule. This final rule amends safety standards related to use of the locomotive horn to provide regulatory relief from the required pattern of sounding the locomotive horn in two long blasts, one short blast, and one long blast for locomotive engineers operating trains, locomotive consists, or individual locomotives that have stopped in close proximity to a public highway-rail grade crossing. This final rule allows locomotive engineers to vary the locomotive horn sounding pattern to one single blast of the horn as they enter the nearby public highway-rail grade crossing.

candidates.title: Chemical shipments percolate in latest rail data
candidates.excerpt: Freight carried by U.S. railroads enjoyed another strong week, according to data from the Association of American Railroads. U.S. weekly rail traffic was 532,462 carloads and intermodal units, up 4.2% compared with the same week a year ago. Total carloads for the week ending August 22 came to 235,885 units, up 3.2%, while intermodal volume was 296,577 containers and trailers, up 5% on 2025. Seven of 10 carload commodity groups posted an increase compared with the same week in 2025. They included metallic ores and metals , 9.5%; chemicals, up 6% after several down weeks; and grain, up 9%. Motor vehicles and parts slipped 10.4% for the week. For the first 33 weeks of 2026, U.S. railroads reported cumulative volume of 7,511,910 carloads, up 2.7%, and 9,301,986 intermodal units, up 3.8% y/y. Total combined traffic was 16,813,896 carloads and intermodal units, an increase of 3.3% from the previous year. candidates.title: Union Pacific, Norfolk Southern defend rail merger application as STB review advances
candidates.excerpt: Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern said Thursday that their proposed combination has met the Surface Transportation Board’s threshold requirements, urging regulators to reject opponents’ preliminary challenges and proceed with a full review of the transaction. In a response filing, the railroads said their application contains extensive evidence developed over months of work and provides the STB with sufficient information to determine that the merger is consistent with the public interest. The companies characterized the opposition’s challenges as efforts to derail the transaction before the board can evaluate its proposed benefits in full. The filing follows the STB’s Aug. 18 issuance of a procedural schedule for the merger proceeding. candidates.title: Abandoned vans lead deputies to $123K in Brooks shoes from BNSF boxcar theft
candidates.excerpt: Update, Aug. 26: BNSF responded after publication, calling organized cargo theft a growing threat to public safety and the U.S. supply chain. California deputies recovered more than $123,000 in Brooks running shoes after a suspected BNSF train boxcar burglary. San Bernardino County deputies found two abandoned vans while traveling toward Ludlow on Aug. 22. BNSF Railway Police had requested assistance after a train made an emergency stop nearby. Authorities had noticed three vehicles near the train under suspicious circumstances. Deputies inspected both vans and discovered numerous boxes inside each vehicle. BNSF Police confirmed the boxes came from the boxcar, according to the San Bernardino County Sheriff’s Department announcement. Authorities identified the recovered merchandise as Brooks running shoes. The department valued the footwear at more than $123,000. candidates.title: Deputies recover $150K in New Balance shoes after BNSF boxcar burglary
candidates.excerpt: California deputies recovered more than $150,000 in New Balance shoes after reports of people breaking into BNSF Railroad boxcars. The San Bernardino County Sheriff’s Department’s Barstow Station announced the recovery Aug. 24. Authorities arrested Leonardo Martinez Navarre, 29, after he fled a traffic stop near Daggett. Daggett is an unincorporated community in San Bernardino County, about 10 miles east of Barstow. Barstow sits in California’s Mojave Desert, along Interstate 15 between Los Angeles and Las Vegas. The call came at about 7:04 a.m. Monday near westbound Interstate 40 in Daggett. While heading toward the location, Barstow Station personnel saw a vehicle matching the suspects’ description. The driver headed west on I-40 before officers initiated a stop. Navarre exited and ran, according to the sheriff’s department. candidates.title: Rail consultant returns to lead South Carolina short line
candidates.excerpt: Palmetto Railways announced the appointment of Tarek Ravenel as president and chief executive officer. The move by the state-owned transportation company is effective Sept. 8, 2026. Ravenel, who earlier spent a decade at the railway, brings a “proven track record in transportation and infrastructure leadership and will steer the organization into its next phase of growth, investment and economic impact across South Carolina,” the company said in a release. Ravenel succeeds Patrick McCrory, who has served as president and CEO since 2022. Based in Charleston, Palmetto connects with CSX (NASDAQ: CSX) and Norfolk Southern (NYSE: NSC), operating 90 miles of track in five counties, including at the Port of Charleston. It is developing a 25-mile industrial rail line serving Camp Hall Commerce Park and other industrial properties in Berkeley County.
